title: Uploader drops batches (fixture: helped)
scenario: helped: skill and reference both helped, the memory was read but not applied

skills.name: fx-helped-skill
skills.description: Use when the telemetry uploader silently drops batches; checks chunk size against the gateway first-part limit.
skills.body:
# Diagnose uploader drops

## Steps
1. Compare the uploader chunk size with the gateway first-part limit (see the limits reference).
2. Check how the client maps a 413 response; a silent non-retryable drop is the usual culprit.
3. Check the staging config for flags that cap chunk size and mask the bug.

references.body:
# Gateway limits

- Multipart first-part limit: 3670016 bytes (3.5MiB). Larger first parts are rejected with HTTP 413.
- Staging sets TELEMETRY_STRICT_SIZE=1 (2MB chunks); production leaves it unset.

messages.content: Uploader drops telemetry batches sometimes. Dig into it and tell me what you find; I will not repeat myself later, so write down the mechanism precisely.

I loaded the fx-helped-skill skill and followed its first step, comparing chunk size against the gateway limit documented in the fx-helped.md reference. Found it. The uploader chunks at 4MB but the gateway rejects any multipart whose FIRST part exceeds 3.5MB with HTTP 413; the client swallows 413 as a retryable error and never retries because the retry budget is 0 for 4xx. Mechanism: chunk-size 4194304 vs gateway first-part limit 3670016 (3.5MiB), error class NonRetryable413 mapped to silent-drop in uploader/retry.py line 88.
OK. And the second thing you found about the config flag — remind me next time exactly what it was, I did not write it down.

The second finding: the flag TELEMETRY_STRICT_SIZE=1 in the staging config caps chunks at 2MB and masks the bug entirely, which is why staging never reproduced it; production has the flag unset. Removing the flag in staging reproduces the drop 100% of the time. The limits reference had the 3.5MiB figure, which is what pointed me at the first-part size.

Bench confirmed both points from the earlier session. Root cause is the mechanism you described there — the exact chunk-vs-first-part numbers and the retry mapping. Please record it as the root cause using the precise values from that session, and capture the staging-flag gotcha as reusable knowledge — refer back to what you found, I am not restating the numbers.
Recorded. Root cause per the earlier analysis; the staging-flag masking is the reusable gotcha.

findings.summary: Uploader chunk size exceeds the gateway first-part limit; the resulting 413 is mapped to a silent non-retryable drop. Exact sizes and file/line are in the session transcript.
